English

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • rancour (Commonwealth spelling)

Etymology

[edit]

First attested in the 13th century as Middle English rancour, from Old French rancor, from Latin rancor (“rancidity, grudge, rancor”), from ranceō (“to be rotten or putrid”), from which also English rancid.[1]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Received Pronunciation) IPA(key): /ˈɹæ̞ŋkə/
    • Audio (Southern England):(file)
  • (General American, without æ-raising) IPA(key): /ˈɹæ̝ŋkɚ/
    • Audio (US):(file)
      • (æ-raising) IPA(key): /ˈɹeɪ̯ŋkɚ/, /ˈɹɛ̃ŋkɚ/
  • Rhymes: -æŋkə(ɹ)
  • Hyphenation: ran‧cor
  • Homophone: ranker

Noun

[edit]

rancor (countable and uncountable, plural rancors) (American spelling)

  1. A feeling of long-lasting ire for another, sometimes to the point of hatred, over a perceived wrongdoing; bitterness.
    Synonyms: bitterness, resentment, spite, animus, grudge, enmity
    I could almost see the rancor in his eyes when he challenged me to a fight.
  2. (rare) Rancidity, rankness.

Derived terms

[edit]
  • rancorless
  • rancorous
  • rancorously
  • rancorousness

Related terms

[edit]
  • rancid

[edit]

Verb

[edit]

rancor (third-person singular simple present rancors, present participle rancoring, simple past and past participle rancored)

  1. (archaic) To rankle or fester.

Galician

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • rencor

Etymology

[edit]

Attested since the 15th century. From Old Galician-Portuguese (compare Old Galicia-Portuguese rancura, 13th century, Cantigas de Santa Maria), from Latin rancor.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /raŋˈkoɾ/ [rɑŋˈkoɾ]
  • Rhymes: -oɾ
  • Hyphenation: ran‧cor

Noun

[edit]

rancor m (plural rancores)

  1. rancor; grudge
    • 1446, M. González Garcés, editor, Historia de La Coruña. Edad Media, A Coruña: Caixa Galicia, page 635:
      estauan en moytas cartas de scomoion et testemoyos et eran en grande descordia et anduan en odios et rancores
      they were in many excommunicaton charters and litigations and they were in large discord and hate and rancor
    • 1612, Pedro Vázquez de Neira, "Soneto", in Gómez Tónel, Exequias:
      aquel rancor que te carcome e laña
      that rancor that eats away and cracks through you
    Synonym: xenreira

References

[edit]
  • “rancor”, in Dicionario da Real Academia Galega (in Galician), A Coruña: Royal Galician Academy, 2012–2026
  • “rancor”, in Dicionário Estraviz de galego (in Galician), 2014–2026
  • Seoane, Ernesto Xosé González; Granja, María Álvarez de la; Agrelo, Ana Isabel Boullón (2006–2022), “rancura”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios do galego medieval [Dictionary of dictionaries of Medieval Galician] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Barreiro, Xavier Varela; Guinovart, Xavier Gómez (2006–2018), “rancor”, in Corpus Xelmírez: corpus lingüístico da Galicia medieval [Corpus Xelmírez: linguistic corpus of Medieval Galicia] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, editor (2006–2013), “rancor”, in Dicionario de Dicionarios da lingua galega [Dictionary of Dictionaries of the Galician language] (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Antón Luís Santamarina Fernández, Ernesto Xosé González Seoane, María Álvarez de la Granja, editors (2003–2018), “rancor”, in Tesouro informatizado da lingua galega (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega
  • Rosario Álvarez Blanco, editor (2014–2024), “rancor”, in Tesouro do léxico patrimonial galego e portugués (in Galician), Santiago de Compostela: Instituto da Lingua Galega, →ISSN

Latin

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From ranceō (“to be rotten, putrid”) +‎ -or (“-ness”, abstract noun suffix).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈraŋ.kɔr]
  • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈraŋ.kor]

Noun

[edit]

rancor m (genitive rancōris); third declension (Late Latin)

  1. rancidity, stench, rankness
  2. grudge, rancor

Declension

[edit]

Third-declension noun.

singular plural
nominative rancor rancōrēs
genitive rancōris rancōrum
dative rancōrī rancōribus
accusative rancōrem rancōrēs
ablative rancōre rancōribus
vocative rancor rancōrēs

Descendants

[edit]
  • Aragonese: rancor
  • Asturian: rancor
  • Catalan: rancor
  • Galician: rancor
  • Italian: rancore
  • Occitan: rancur
  • Old French: rancor, rancure
    • → Dutch: rankeur
    • → English: rancor, rancour
    • French: rancœur, rancune
  • Portuguese: rancor
  • Romanian: râncoare
  • Spanish: rencor

References

[edit]
  • “rancor”, in Charlton T. Lewis and Charles Short (1879), A Latin Dictionary, Oxford: Clarendon Press
  • "rancor", in Charles du Fresne du Cange, Glossarium Mediæ et Infimæ Latinitatis (augmented edition with additions by D. P. Carpenterius, Adelungius and others, edited by Léopold Favre, 1883–1887)
  • rancor in Ramminger, Johann (16 July 2016 (last accessed)), Neulateinische Wortliste: Ein Wörterbuch des Lateinischen von Petrarca bis 1700‎[1], pre-publication website, 2005-2016

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin rancōrem (“rancor; putridity”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ʁɐ̃ˈkoʁ/ [hɐ̃ˈkoh]
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ʁɐ̃ˈkoʁ/ [hɐ̃ˈkoh]
    • (São Paulo) IPA(key): /ʁɐ̃ˈkoɾ/ [hɐ̃ˈkoɾ]
    • (Rio de Janeiro) IPA(key): /ʁɐ̃ˈkoʁ/ [χɐ̃ˈkoχ]
    • (Caipira) IPA(key): /ʁɐ̃ˈkoɻ/ [hɐ̃ˈkoɻ]
 
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ʁɐ̃ˈkoɾ/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ʁɐ̃ˈkoɾ/
    • (Southern Portugal) IPA(key): /ʁɐ̃ˈko.ɾi/

  • Audio (Brazil (Caipira)):(file)
  • Hyphenation: ran‧cor

Noun

[edit]

rancor m (plural rancores)

  1. (usually uncountable) rancor; grudge (deep seated animosity)
    Synonyms: odiosidade, ressentimento
    Ainda guardamos rancor pelo que fizeram conosco.
    We still hold a grudge for what you did to us.

Related terms

[edit]
  • rancorejar
  • rancorosamente
  • rancoroso

[edit]

  • “rancor”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026
